title: The Conductor Lab
summary: Probe a charged metal sphere, test which set-ups a hollow conductor shields, and reduce a field with a dielectric slab.
subject: physics
concepts: Field and potential of a charged conductor
learningOutcome: The student can give the field inside, at and outside a charged conductor, say when a cavity is shielded, and find the field inside a dielectric.

levels.title: The charged sphere
levels.adds: Baseline: inside a conductor E = 0, just outside E = kq/R², and the potential is constant throughout (Ex 2.4).
hints: All the charge sits on the surface, so a Gaussian sphere inside encloses none: E = 0 inside.
Outside the sphere acts like a point charge at its centre: E = kq/r², with r from the centre.
The field jumps at the surface, but the potential kq/R is continuous and constant inside.

levels.title: Shielding
levels.adds: New idea: an empty cavity is shielded from charges outside, but a charge inside a cavity still gives a field outside (Example 2.7).
hints: Charges outside induce surface charge that cancels their field in the conductor and in an empty cavity.
A charge inside the cavity induces charge on the walls and the outer surface, so there is a field outside.

levels.title: A dielectric slab
levels.adds: New idea: the polarised molecules reduce the field inside a dielectric by the factor K.
hints: The molecules line up with the field, giving induced surface charges that oppose the applied field.
The net field inside is E = E₀ / K.
Polar molecules (such as water) have permanent dipoles; non-polar ones get induced dipoles in a field.

misconceptions: There is a field inside a charged conductor
The potential inside a charged conductor is zero
Shielding works from the inside out as well
A dielectric increases the field inside it
